name: MoE Writing Rubric — Module F (16584)
content:
WRITING RUBRIC — Israeli Ministry of Education
Module G (16582) and Module F external (16584) — as of Winter 2020

Maximum score: 40 points across 4 criteria.
In-between grades are allowed (e.g. 7 pts on a 10-pt criterion).

========================================================
CRITERION 1 — CONTENT AND ORGANIZATION (max 8 pts)
========================================================

8 — CORRECT:
  • fully on topic
  • fully developed (main idea AND supporting details)
  • all elements of the task are addressed
  • information is relevant
  • content is understood
  • task is well organized and coherent

5 — PARTIALLY CORRECT:
  • partially on topic
  • partially developed (main idea OR supporting details)
  • partially addresses elements of the task
  • information is partially relevant
  • content is partially understood
  • task is partially organized and coherent

2 — MINIMALLY CORRECT:
  • minimally on topic
  • minimally developed (main idea or supporting details)
  • minimally addresses elements of the task
  • information is minimally relevant
  • content is minimally understood
  • task is minimally organized and coherent

0 — INCORRECT:
  • not on topic
  • not developed (main idea or supporting details)
  • elements are not addressed, due to misunderstanding
  • information is not relevant, due to misunderstanding
  • content is not understood
  • task is not organized and not coherent

Partial-credit cases:
  • Student is asked to present advantages and/or disadvantages of a subject AND express their opinion, but does not express their opinion.
  • Wrong tense (e.g. an event that should be described in the past is described in the future).
  • Student states an opinion but contradicts it later in the task.

Minimal-credit cases:
  • Irrelevance clearly reflects misunderstanding of the subject (e.g. "pastimes" → "past times"; "after-school activities" → activities after graduating from school). Zero or a minimal number of points for Content, but marks are still given for the remaining criteria.
  • If a partial reference to the task changes the essence of the task → ZERO for the entire task (e.g. asked to describe "a nice thing someone did for him", but only describes "a nice thing" such as a car).
  • Poor language, organization or vocabulary (misuse of electronic dictionaries or otherwise) making the task almost incomprehensible → 1–2 marks for Content; the remaining criteria will also be very low. If completely incomprehensible → ZERO for the entire task.

Organization deductions — deduct according to severity, but NOT more than 50% of the criterion, when:
  • the student writes in list form
  • the student writes in letter format (date, Dear X, signature) in a task that is not a letter
  • the student begins with "Hi" / "Hi. My name is… / I live in… / I study at X school / I am seventeen years old" when it is irrelevant to the topic or task (note there may be cases where this opening IS appropriate)
  • whole ideas are repeated (e.g. "I love my job… I like my job very much… I enjoy my job")
  • there is no introduction and/or conclusion
  • ideas are expressed in a disorganized and confusing manner

========================================================
CRITERION 2 — VOCABULARY (max 10 pts)
========================================================

10 — CORRECT:
  • correct use of varied and rich vocabulary
  • appropriate use of instances of language chunks and phrases (phrasal verbs, collocations)
  • correct use of connecting words or phrases
  • use of appropriate register

6 — PARTIALLY CORRECT:
  • correct use of basic, appropriate vocabulary
  • partially appropriate use of instances of chunks and phrases
  • partial and correct use of connecting words or phrases
  • occasional use of inappropriate register

3 — MINIMALLY CORRECT:
  • minimally correct use of basic, appropriate vocabulary
  • minimally appropriate instances of chunks and phrases
  • minimal use of connecting words or phrases
  • consistent use of inappropriate register

0 — INCORRECT:
  • incorrect use of words
  • inappropriate use of chunks and phrases
  • no use of connecting words or phrases
  • consistent use of inappropriate register

Notes:
  • Students are expected to use a variety of low-frequency words and appropriate connectors (words and/or phrases). As of Winter 2020 students must show productive knowledge of Band 3 vocabulary in their compositions.
  • Deduct up to 3 points for each of: vocabulary that is correct but repeated (e.g. "very" and "much" over and over); slang or abbreviations such as 4U (for you), BTW (by the way).

========================================================
CRITERION 3 — LANGUAGE USE (max 16 pts)
========================================================

16 — CORRECT:
  • correct use of basic tenses and/or language structures
  • correct use of advanced language structures
  • correct word order
  • correct use of parts of speech, pronouns and prepositions

10 — PARTIALLY CORRECT:
  • correct use of basic tenses and/or language structures
  • incorrect or no use of advanced language structures
  • occasional instances of incorrect word order
  • occasional incorrect use of parts of speech, pronouns and prepositions

5 — MINIMALLY CORRECT:
  • minimally correct use of basic tenses and/or language structures
  • incorrect or no use of advanced language structures
  • minimally correct word order
  • minimally correct use of parts of speech, pronouns and prepositions

0 — INCORRECT:
  • incorrect use of basic tenses and/or language structures
  • incorrect or no use of advanced language structures
  • incorrect word order
  • incorrect use of parts of speech, pronouns and prepositions

Notes:
  • Basic language: students are expected to formulate sentences correctly using the basic tenses (present simple/progressive, past simple, future simple), and to make correct use of modals, parts of speech, determiners, singular and plural nouns.
  • Advanced structures: passive, conditionals, inversions, verb complements (gerunds, infinitives), relative clauses, reported/indirect speech, indirect questions, perfect tenses, temporal clauses and other complex sentence structures. Students should correctly use a variety of AT LEAST 3 advanced structures. If the task uses basic language and structures correctly but makes no use of any advanced forms, deduct up to 6 points.

========================================================
CRITERION 4 — MECHANICS (max 6 pts)
========================================================

6 — CORRECT use of:
  • spelling
  • punctuation
  • capitalization
  • paragraphing
  and no run-on sentences

4 — PARTIALLY CORRECT use of the above, with some run-on sentences.
2 — MINIMALLY CORRECT use of the above, with frequent run-on sentences.
0 — INCORRECT use of the above, with consistent run-on sentences.

Notes:
  • The maximum deduction for SPELLING ALONE is 3 points. When problematic spelling is accompanied by errors of punctuation, capitalization, paragraphing and/or run-on sentences, more points may be deducted.
  • Unlike Module C, Module F/G students ARE expected to paragraph, and may be penalized for not doing so.

========================================================
GENERAL RULES
========================================================

Copying from the reading passage (unseen), when its topic is similar to the writing task:
  • Writing task copied in its entirety from the reading passage → ZERO for the entire task.
  • Substantial parts copied → count ONLY the words written in the student's own language, then apply the length-deduction table below. Use of individual vocabulary items from the unseen passage is acceptable.

ZERO the entire composition when ANY of:
  • fewer than 50 words
  • totally unrelated to the topic
  • content cannot be understood at all
  • copied from the Internet (report a חשד with the URL of the site)

Word-count EXCLUDES:
  • letter elements (date, Dear X, Yours / Love and kisses, signature)
  • the instruction sentence copied word for word (but if the student incorporates it correctly by changing pronouns and making other adjustments → counts as part of the task)
  • substantial parts copied word for word from the reading passage
  • a title (students are not required to write one)

Length evaluation procedure:
  1. First evaluate the task on merit as if it were the right length.
  2. Then apply the length deduction, starting with the Content criterion and, if necessary, continuing to the additional criteria.

Length-deduction tables:

  Module G internal and external (required 120–140 words):
    110–119 → -2   |   100–109 → -4   |   90–99 → -8   |   80–89 → -12
    70–79   → -16  |   60–69   → -18  |   50–59 → -20  |   <50   → -40

  Module F external (required 100–120 words):
    90–99 → -2   |   80–89 → -4   |   70–79 → -8   |   60–69 → -12
    50–59 → -16  |   40–49 → -18  |   <40  → -40

========================================================
OUTPUT INSTRUCTIONS
========================================================

• Per-criterion score: integer between 0 and the criterion's max (in-between values allowed, e.g. 7 on a 10-pt criterion).
• Per-criterion feedback: 1–3 short sentences, in ENGLISH.
• Overall score: a string in the form "X/40" (e.g. "33/40"), scoring the task ON MERIT as if it were the right length. Do NOT apply the length deduction yourself — the system applies it deterministically from the length-deduction table after you answer, and applying it twice would double-penalize the student.
• Overall feedback: 2–4 sentences in ENGLISH — strengths, weaknesses, what the student should work on next.
• Every issue comment must be in ENGLISH and must name the problem only (the report colors it by criterion already) — e.g. "missing article", "subject-verb agreement", not "Mechanics: missing article".
• If the task is one of the auto-zero cases above (off-topic / incomprehensible / copied), set all criterion scores to 0 and explain why in overall_feedback. The under-50-words case is handled by the length deduction — still grade on merit.
